meta.disclaimer: Course titles, prerequisite wording, and descriptions in this planner were seeded from the official University of Michigan LSA Mathematics undergraduate course pages on July 1, 2026. Official University of Michigan LSA, Mathematics Department, and Course Guide information controls for enrollment and prerequisite decisions.

courses.title: External prerequisite referenced by Math 423
courses.description: Placeholder node for the programming prerequisite referenced on the official Math 423 page.
courses.notes: Referenced by the official Math 423 prerequisite text as 'EECS 183 or equivalent.'

courses.title: External prerequisite referenced by Math 526
courses.description: Placeholder node for the alternative EECS prerequisite referenced on the official Math 526 page.
courses.notes: Referenced by the official Math 526 prerequisite text as 'Math 525 or EECS 501.'

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: Introductory calculus focused on functions, derivatives, and a first introduction to integration.

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.description: Continuation of the standard calculus sequence covering integration techniques, series, and introductory differential equations.
courses.notes: Graph prerequisite simplified to MATH 115; the official text also allows AP credit.

courses.title: Applied Honors Calculus II
courses.description: An honors-oriented alternative to Math 116 with more emphasis on science applications and theory.
courses.notes: Official prerequisite is AP exam based, so no incoming graph edge is stored.
courses.prerequisite_text: Score of 4 or 5 on Advanced Placement AB or BC Calculus exam

courses.title: Honors Calculus II
courses.description: A rigorous continuation of the honors calculus sequence that develops deeper theoretical foundations.
courses.notes: Official prerequisite references Math 185, which is not included in this focused seed.
courses.prerequisite_text: Permission of honors advisor or Math 185

courses.title: Calculus of Several Variables
courses.description: A multivariable calculus alternative to Math 215 with an emphasis on concepts and applications.

courses.title: Applied Linear Algebra
courses.description: A linear algebra course centered on matrix methods, concepts, and applications.

courses.title: Multivariable & Vector Calculus
courses.description: The standard multivariable calculus course in the main introductory mathematics sequence.

courses.title: Introduction to Differential Equations
courses.description: An applications-focused differential equations course for science and engineering students.

courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.description: The proof-oriented linear algebra course that anchors many upper-level pure and applied math paths.

courses.title: Explorations in Calculus (IBL)
courses.description: An inquiry-based, theory-leaning calculus course designed to prepare students for honors multivariable work.
courses.notes: The Honors Sequences page also describes Math 276 as part of the honors seminar mathematics sequence.
courses.prerequisite_text: Math 115 or AP Credit or permission of math advisor; highly recommended for students who have taken Math 275

courses.title: Honors Multivariable & Vector Calculus (IBL)
courses.description: The honors multivariable calculus option with a more theoretical approach than Math 215.
courses.prerequisite_text: Math 156, 186, 276, or permission of honors advisor

courses.title: Honors Differential Equations
courses.description: The honors differential equations course in the honors calculus sequence.

courses.title: Honors Mathematics II
courses.description: Part of the most theoretical honors mathematics sequence, with strong preparation for advanced analysis and algebra.
courses.notes: Official prerequisite references Math 295, which is not included in this focused seed.

courses.title: Applied Modern Algebra
courses.description: A proof-oriented algebra course that ties abstract structures to applications such as automata and coding.

courses.title: Mathematics of Blockchains and Cryptocurrencies
courses.description: A course on the mathematical and algorithmic ideas behind blockchains, cryptography, and related systems.
courses.notes: The official prerequisite wording is advisory. The graph stores a planner-friendly math-background approximation and leaves programming preparation in the exact text field.
courses.prerequisite_text: Math prerequisites (advisory): One previous college math class in discrete math or linear algebra or abstract algebra (eg. EECS 203, MATH 214, MATH 217, MATH 275, MATH 312). Programming prerequisites: Fundamental concepts of programming in a high-level language, preferably Python (eg. COMPFOR 131; PHYSICS 104; or EECS 183 with prior Python knowledge).

courses.title: Differential Equations
courses.description: A proof-aware differential equations course for students who have already studied linear algebra.
courses.notes: Graph structure is a planner-friendly summary of the official wording.

courses.title: Principles of Analysis (IBL)
courses.description: An introduction to rigorous analysis and proof that develops the ideas underlying calculus.
courses.notes: The graph uses a simplified summary; check the exact prerequisite wording for the official logic.
courses.prerequisite_text: Math 215 and 217 or 205 or 285, or permission of instructor

courses.title: Introduction to Modern Algebra (IBL)
courses.description: A proof-focused introduction to abstract algebra and mathematical structures such as groups, rings, and fields.

courses.title: Mathematics of Finance
courses.description: An introduction to mathematical finance focused on derivative pricing models and their probabilistic foundations.
courses.prerequisite_text: Math 217 and Math 425 or 525, and EECS 183 or equivalent

courses.title: Compound Interest and Life Insurance
courses.description: An actuarial-oriented course on interest theory and valuation of deposits, annuities, and bonds.

courses.title: Introduction to Probability
courses.description: A probability course covering both theory and applications across discrete and continuous settings.

courses.title: Advanced Calculus I
courses.description: A rigorous analysis course centered on proofs, structure, and the foundations of calculus.
courses.notes: The official prerequisite wording is example-based. The graph uses MATH 217 and MATH 412 as a planner-friendly approximation.
courses.prerequisite_text: Previous exposure to abstract mathematics, e.g. MATH 217 and 412

courses.title: Mathematical Models
courses.description: An applied modeling course that emphasizes translating real problems into mathematics and analyzing them.

courses.title: Introduction to Combinatorics
courses.description: An introductory combinatorics course covering counting methods and graph theory fundamentals.
courses.notes: The official prerequisite allows additional linear algebra alternatives and instructor permission.
courses.prerequisite_text: Linear Algebra (one of Math 214, 217, 296, 417, or 419) or permission of instructor

courses.title: Introduction to Stochastic Analysis for Finance
courses.description: A continuation of mathematical finance into stochastic calculus and continuous-time models.

courses.title: Probability Theory
courses.description: An introductory graduate-level probability course focused on core concepts, major results, and proofs.
courses.prerequisite_text: One semester of multivariable calculus (205, 215, 285 or equivalent) and one semester of analysis (351, 451, or equivalent), OR graduate standing.

courses.title: Discrete State Stochastic Processes
courses.description: A second probability course on stochastic processes in discrete and continuous time.

courses.title: Combinatorics and Graph Theory
courses.description: A beginning graduate combinatorics course with emphasis on graph theory and related structures.
courses.prerequisite_text: Math 465 or equivalent experience with abstract mathematics.

courses.title: Combinatorial Theory
courses.description: A beginning graduate combinatorics course emphasizing enumerative and algebraic techniques.
courses.prerequisite_text: Math 465 or equivalent experience with abstract mathematics.
